title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Auditorium on 1969-06-27
lineage: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT > DAT > ZA2 > Soundforge > .wav > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a smoking 1969 set featuring rare Slewfoot, a soaring Dark Star>St. Stephen>Eleven, and a stellar Dire Wolf with Bobby on vocals.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid soundboard tape that delivers clear balance despite occasional mix quirks (notably on Slewfoot and the early drum tracks). Musically the show swings from laid‑back country numbers into an explosive psychedelic second half, highlighted by a smoking Dark Star>St. Stephen>Eleven sequence, Jerry’s pedal‑steel work on Slewfoot and Dire Wolf, and Bobby’s confident lead vocals. Overall energy is high and the setlist showcases the Dead in transition between their folk‑rock roots and emerging country‑rock direction.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.25/5 across 16 reviews; the majority praise both performance and recording, with only minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced soundboard tape; some reviewers note mix issues on Slewfoot and a slightly off drum feel in the first few songs, but overall crisp.

standout_songs: Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven
show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with relaxed, country‑tinged material (Slewfoot, Mama Tried, High Time, Dupree's, Me & My Uncle) then shifts into a high‑energy psychedelic second half highlighted by Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven and the surprising turn to Green Green Grass of Home before closing with Baby Blue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Frequent pedal‑steel work on Slewfoot, Dire Wolf and Green Green Grass; praised for tone and added country flavor.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a deep Lovelight jam during Dark Star and generally solid bass foundation throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby takes lead vocals on Dire Wolf (and other songs) with confidence; his performance is singled out as a highlight.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s drippy organ chords are mentioned, especially on Baby Blue; keyboards add a gospelly texture in the encore.
band_member_comments.Drums: Early portion described as slightly off‑beat, then praised for flowing double‑drum work later; one reviewer suggests Bill and Mickey may have been mixed with an extra drummer on the first tunes.
